new_scholarship.name: Oberlin Commitment Scholarship
new_scholarship.deadline: Aid deadline published annually; aid materials arrive with the admission notification
new_scholarship.application_period: All admitted students are reviewed for merit scholarships automatically; no separate application is required.
new_scholarship.application_method: Automatic - reviewed for merit scholarships upon admission, no separate application
new_scholarship.description: The Oberlin Commitment Scholarship is a renewable $10,000 award granted to every student who enrols in the College of Arts and Sciences and/or the Conservatory of Music. It is granted to all students - domestic, international and transfer - and is renewable each year. Oberlin additionally publishes three merit-based scholarships for which eligible international students may be considered.
new_scholarship.best_fit: Any student enrolling at Oberlin in the College of Arts and Sciences or Conservatory of Music, including international applicants, with no separate application required.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Open to all students enrolling in the College of Arts and Sciences and/or Conservatory of Music, explicitly including international and transfer students. Awarded automatically on enrolment, renewable each year.
eligibility: Enrol in the College of Arts and Sciences and/or the Conservatory of Music at Oberlin
Domestic, international and transfer students are all eligible
No separate application is required; all admitted students are reviewed automatically
coverage: $10,000 per year toward tuition, renewable each year at Oberlin
benefits: Renewable $10,000 Oberlin Commitment Scholarship for all students in the College of Arts and Sciences and/or Conservatory of Music
Granted in addition to need-based aid

Three separate merit scholarships are open to eligible international students: Eduardo Chivangu Mondlane Scholarship (up to $10,000), Ambassador Edwin O. Reischauer Scholarship (up to $10,000), and the Oberlin College Office of Admissions Mondlane selection process
requirements: Enrol in the College of Arts and Sciences and/or Conservatory of Music
new_scholarship.selection_notes: Minimum aid award for every student enrolling at Oberlin. Oberlin is need-aware rather than need-blind for international applicants, and the international financial aid budget is explicitly limited.
new_scholarship.notes: Oberlin states it meets 100% of demonstrated need for all international students who apply for aid, with the average aid package covering about two-thirds of the cost of attendance.

programme_detail_official.funding_label: $10,000 per year, renewable, automatic for all College of Arts and Sciences and Conservatory of Music enrollees
benefits: Oberlin Commitment Scholarship: renewable $10,000 for all students enrolling in the College of Arts and Sciences and/or Conservatory of Music
Eduardo Chivangu Mondlane Scholarship: up to $10,000, for any citizen of a sub-Saharan African country applying to the College of Arts and Sciences, no supplementary materials required

Ambassador Edwin O. Reischauer Scholarship: up to $10,000, for any Japanese national admitted to the College of Arts and Sciences, for students educated in Japan committed to international understanding

programme_detail_official.citizenship_residency: The Commitment Scholarship has no citizenship restriction; the Mondlane and Reischauer awards are nationality-restricted
programme_detail_official.international_eligibility: Open to international students. Oberlin is need-aware for international applicants, meaning financial circumstances are considered in admissions decisions, and approximately 8-10 percent of international applicants are admitted in a typical year. Applicants able to contribute at least $35,000 USD per year are the most competitive.

application_readiness_checklist: Apply to Oberlin - no separate merit scholarship application is required
If you want need-based aid, submit the CSS Profile (code 1587) or the ISAFA in your applicant portal once it appears
Upload supporting financial documentation such as tax returns or bank statements
Submit everything by the published aid deadline so your package arrives with your admission notification
If you are a citizen of a sub-Saharan African country, note the Mondlane Scholarship requires no supplementary materials
If you are a Japanese national, note the Reischauer Scholarship
common_rejection_risks: Missing the annual aid deadline and losing the package, or losing need-based aid eligibility for later years
Expecting the Commitment Scholarship outside the College of Arts and Sciences or Conservatory of Music
Assuming the $10,000 Commitment Scholarship covers living costs
Overlooking that Oberlin is need-aware, so financial circumstances affect the admission decision
estimated_uncovered_costs: Living expenses and accommodation beyond the Commitment Scholarship
Books, transportation, health insurance and incidental charges, which Oberlin states are not included in its tuition, housing and food costs
Any portion of demonstrated need not met if aid was not applied for at the time of admission
document_audit: CSS Profile (code 1587) or ISAFA for need-based aid
No award-specific documents for the Commitment Scholarship
